newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on plantings, wheat slide.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on plantings, wheat slide.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended lower on Wednesday, hit by a late slide in wheat futures and ideas drier weather this week would allow for corn planting progress, traders said.
"Our corn (seeding) is on time. It's being planted," said Jason Roose, analyst with U.S. Commodities in Iowa. "Acres are still a pretty good size."
Cool but mainly dry weather in key Midwest corn growing areas was expected, forecasters said. Grain dealers said planting was under way and farmers hoped soils would warm enough for germination.

Corn values had drawn strength recently from ideas cool, damp weather would slow seeding. But USDA Monday said seven percent of U.S. corn was planted as of Sunday, slightly behind seven a year ago and equal to the five-year average of seven percent.
Corn futures ended three to 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower with May down 2-3/4 at $2.98-1/2.
Nearby contracts were pressured by losses in wheat tied to predictions for rain in Europe this weekend, traders said.
They also noted bear spreading. Smith Barney spread at least eight million bushels Dec/May at 15 to 17 cents, premium May.
Louis Dreyfus spread five million July/May and Continental Grain spread two million December/May, pit sources said.
On the day, Refco Inc sold four million bushels July and 1.5 million December, traders said, and Tenco Inc sold one million July.

In options trade, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer sold 1,500 July $2.90 puts at 7-3/4 to 7-1/2 cents, FIMAT Futures sold 1,200 July $3.00 puts at 12-1/2 to 12 cents and FIMAT Futures sold 1,600 July $2.90 puts at seven to 7-1/4 cents, floor sources said.
Corn volume was estimated by CBOT at 50,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 53,545.
